evidence_packet.title: GCHQ intern who took data home loses bid to cut sentence
evidence_packet.lead: Hasaan Arshad breached security rules by transferring material from a GCHQ computer system in 2022
evidence_packet.summary: Hasaan Arshad breached security rules by transferring material from a GCHQ computer system in 2022
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A GCHQ intern who was jailed for endangering national security by taking top secret data home has lost a bid to reduce his jail term Manchester University computer science student Hasaan Arshad breached tight security rules when he used his mobile phone to remove material from a computer system at GCHQ and transfer it to his private computer on 24 August 2022 The 26-year-old was jailed for seven-and-a-half years after he admitted an offence under the Computer Misuse Act and two charges of making an indecent photograph of a child On Thursday Lady Justice Cockerill refused Arshad permission to challenge his sentence, saying there were no arguable grounds that the sentencing judge was wrong 'I was not living a normal life, I was surviving' Published 18 hours ago Home Guard training documents discovered in attic

candidates.lead: Lawrence Johnson is on remand in the prison charged with murdering Alisha Samuels in Newton Heath
candidates.evidence_text: A man who was charged with murdering a 26-year-old woman in Manchester has been attacked in prison Lawrence Johnson, 26, of Dorking Avenue, was held on remand at HMP Liverpool after being charged with the murder of Alisha Samuels, who was found dead in Newton Heath on 15 October Footage seen by the BBC, thought to have been filmed from within the prison at the weekend, shows Johnson being attacked in a cell. In the video, inmates can be heard saying: "Bro, you're getting chopped up. Sit down, bro. Smash him up." A Prison Service spokesperson said the social media post was being investigated, adding "violence will not be tolerated in the prison estate" "Having a phone behind bars is unacceptable and we have ordered the immediate removal of these posts while investigating how this was able to happen," they said Johnson has also been charged with the attempted murder of a man

candidates.summary: The scheme could be up and running by summer 2027 if approved, the council says
candidates.reason: Visible repeat policy allows this item: concrete_story_change:declared. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Учитывать как новую фазу городской политики или public-affairs повестки сегодня.
candidates.lead: The scheme could be up and running by summer 2027 if approved, the council says
candidates.evidence_text: People in Manchester could be travelling around on a fleet of electric scooters next year after plans for a new trial were announced Manchester City Council is putting together proposals for the scheme and said in a report that it could begin in summer 2027, although the authority added it had not yet considered an operator for the e-scooters The plans come off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford which Salford Council said had been a major success A council spokesperson stressed that a decision on whether to proceed with an e-scooter trial had not yet been made, and was conditional on backing from Greater Manchester Police and other groups They said provisional approval had been received from the Department for Transport (DfT) for the council to develop a proposal, and "officers are currently undertaking work to assess future benefits, risks and how an e-scooter scheme could work in practice in Manchester" Summer 2027 was the latest a trial could start in line with DfT requirements for new trials, they added

candidates.evidence_text: People in Manchester could be travelling around on a fleet of electric scooters next year after plans for a new trial were announced Manchester City Council is putting together proposals for the scheme and said in a report that it could begin in summer 2027, although the authority added it had not yet considered an operator for the e-scooters The plans come off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford which Salford Council said had been a major success A council spokesperson stressed that a decision on whether to proceed with an e-scooter trial had not yet been made, and was conditional on backing from Greater Manchester Police and other groups They said provisional approval had been received from the Department for Transport (DfT) for the council to develop a proposal, and "officers are currently undertaking work to assess future benefits, risks and how an e-scooter scheme could work in practice in Manchester" Summer 2027 was the latest a trial could start in line with DfT requirements for new trials, they added

Thomas Reeds, 25, communicated online with a child he believed was 13 between February and April this year, police said Detectives said he used the online platform to 'engage in sexual communications' and later arranged a meeting in Reading, Berkshire. But Reeds, of The Heys in Ashton-under Lyne, Tameside , was met by officers when he arrived on April 8 and subsequently arrested The South East Regional Organised Crime Unit, which carried out the operation, said that following his arrest, officers discovered Reeds was in communication with a number of other children, which he was prohibited from doing by the terms of a Sexual Harm Prevention Order he was A SEROCU spokesperson said: "Digital forensic examination of devices identified evidence of further offending involving children. Investigators established that Reeds possessed 15 indecent images of children." Police said Reeds went on to plead guilty to 18 charges in total

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Development Prince William building new town ‘modelled’ on Greater Manchester suburb It also could be the model for a Manc mega-project Add to preferred sources News Ethan Davies Live News Reporter 06:59, 30 Oct 2026 View 3 Images A central Prince William is building a new town to try to save the UK high street — and it’s inspired by a Greater Manchester suburb Nansledan, on the outskirts of Newquay in Cornwall , is a new town that started construction more than a decade ago. It’s being developed by the Duchy of Cornwall, the private land portfolio run by the Prince of Wales It’s set to be home to 8,000 residents one day, along with a high street that could stop the decline of British town centres. Prime Minister Andy Burnham named regenerating the country’s high streets as a top priority in August, saying they have “become unrecognisable over decade And a key part of Nansledan is an innovative new high street design, with a food hall at its heart that it modelled on Altrincham Market, reports The Economist It’s one of two larger central units — another will be a Tesco supermarket — that will remain within walking distance of Nansledan’s high street, so residents can walk to everything they need and keep the centre vibrant

Paul Wadsworth was killed when his Kawasaki bike hit a BMW X1 on Partington Street in Failsworth , Oldham , on September 9 last yea Mr Wadsworth, a father-of-two who was 46, served with the Royal Regiment of Fusiliers for seven years and had completed tours of Kosovo and Bosnia. He was a well-known and respected supporter of the Royal British Legion in Failsworth, and was a branch chairman An inquest into his death at Rochdale Coroners' Court heard police calculated he was travelling at 63.4mph in a 30mph zone when his bike hit the BMW. The driver of the car, the court heard, was performing a 'creeping manoeuvre' to exit a service road near shops running adjacent t Coroner Julie Mitchell said the BMW 'crept out' and 'breached' the junction as parked cars impeded the driver's view. The views of both the driver and Mr Wadsworth would have been 'impeded' at the time, Ms Mitchell added The court heard a range of traffic calming measures have been implemented on Partington Street since the tragedy. It now has a 20mph limit and features 'traffic cushions' to limit speeds

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Mystery surrounds why respected former soldier killed in motorbike crash was speeding An inquest has been held Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 05:59, 30 Oct 2026 Updated 07:39, 30 Oct 2026 View 3 Images Paul Wadswor Mystery surrounds why a competent motorcyclist was speeding at more than twice the legal limit when he died in a collision with a BMW near his home. Paul Wadsworth was killed when his Kawasaki bike hit a BMW X1 on Partington Street in Failsworth , Oldham , on September 9 last yea Mr Wadsworth, a father-of-two who was 46, served with the Royal Regiment of Fusiliers for seven years and had completed tours of Kosovo and Bosnia. He was a well-known and respected supporter of the Royal British Legion in Failsworth, and was a branch chairman An inquest into his death at Rochdale Coroners' Court heard police calculated he was travelling at 63.4mph in a 30mph zone when his bike hit the BMW. The driver of the car, the court heard, was performing a 'creeping manoeuvre' to exit a service road near shops running adjacent t Coroner Julie Mitchell said the BMW 'crept out' and 'breached' the junction as parked cars impeded the driver's view. The views of both the driver and Mr Wadsworth would have been 'impeded' at the time, Ms Mitchell added The court heard a range of traffic calming measures have been implemented on Partington Street since the tragedy. It now has a 20mph limit and features 'traffic cushions' to limit speeds

candidates.evidence_text: Tyldesley Two teenage boys arrested after Tyldesley crash Officers are looking into the circumstances that led to the arrest Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 18:08, 29 Oct 2026 View Image Elliot Street, Tyldesley Two teenagers were arrested after a stolen van smashed into a bus in Tyldesley. The arrests come after officers were called to reports of a motor theft in the Wigan area around 10pm on Wednesday (October 28) Police spotted the stolen vehicle, leading to a police chase. The pursuit ended on Elliot Street where the van was involved in a collision at around 10.35pm The M.E.N understands the vehicle crashed into a Bee Network Bus on the main road. No injuries have been reported A boy, aged 17, was shortly after arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving and theft of a motor vehicle. Another boy, aged 16, was arrested on suspicion of theft of a motor vehicle Both have been bailed pending further enquiries

When I heard the word cancer it really hit me hard". Add to preferred sourc A grandad from Bury who went to the GP after noticing one symptom was later told by doctors he had a rugby-ball-sized tumour in his abdomen. Lee Bather, from Radcliffe , was diagnosed with kidney cancer in 2018 after the shock discovery of blood in his urine one night before bed The 68-year-old then saw his doctor, who referred him for tests which led to the discovery of a large tumour attached to part of his stomach, bowel and adrenal gland Lee said: "I went to see my GP and was referred immediately for an ultrasound. I could see for myself there was a huge mass on the screen "They said it was the size of a rugby ball and had been growing for around 12 years. When I heard the word cancer it really hit me hard. And the moment when you’re taken down the corridor for surgery not knowing if you’ll wake up and see your family again is really tough." The retired care worker underwent a nine-hour operation to remove the tumour, which was then taken away for research. He is now backing vital research into how type 2 diabetes could increase the risk of the disease

Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Salford Council are funding a £1m overhaul of their environmental services to target fly-tipping, graffiti, and environmental crime hotspots The funding will be used to modernise the service and create ‘visible progress’ on the streets of Salford , according to Deputy Mayor Barbara Bentham Speaking in Kersal, where street sweepers, strimmer teams, a communal skip, and alley-way cleaners descended on the residential area around Stamford road for a ‘day of action’ on Wednesday, September 28, Coun Bentham explained the £839,911 investment will use area-specific data t “Different environments across the city of Salford have different needs dependent on the makeup of that community,” she said. “In my own ward of Claremont, there’s a very high percentage of students. So we know that every September, there’s going to be a lot of mattresses, a lot “Other areas have a higher proportion of big families and might have a need for more bins or collections. Each area has its own set of problems, and it’s looking to address a more direct approach for delivering what that community needs.”

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Mystery surrounds why respected former soldier killed in motorbike crash was speeding An inquest has been held Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 05:59, 30 Oct 2026 Updated 07:39, 30 Oct 2026 View 3 Images Paul Wadswor Mystery surrounds why a competent motorcyclist was speeding at more than twice the legal limit when he died in a collision with a BMW near his home. Paul Wadsworth was killed when his Kawasaki bike hit a BMW X1 on Partington Street in Failsworth , Oldham , on September 9 last yea Mr Wadsworth, a father-of-two who was 46, served with the Royal Regiment of Fusiliers for seven years and had completed tours of Kosovo and Bosnia. He was a well-known and respected supporter of the Royal British Legion in Failsworth, and was a branch chairman An inquest into his death at Rochdale Coroners' Court heard police calculated he was travelling at 63.4mph in a 30mph zone when his bike hit the BMW. The driver of the car, the court heard, was performing a 'creeping manoeuvre' to exit a service road near shops running adjacent t Coroner Julie Mitchell said the BMW 'crept out' and 'breached' the junction as parked cars impeded the driver's view. The views of both the driver and Mr Wadsworth would have been 'impeded' at the time, Ms Mitchell added The court heard a range of traffic calming measures have been implemented on Partington Street since the tragedy. It now has a 20mph limit and features 'traffic cushions' to limit speeds

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Development Prince William building new town ‘modelled’ on Greater Manchester suburb It also could be the model for a Manc mega-project Add to preferred sources News Ethan Davies Live News Reporter 06:59, 30 Oct 2026 View 3 Images A central Prince William is building a new town to try to save the UK high street — and it’s inspired by a Greater Manchester suburb Nansledan, on the outskirts of Newquay in Cornwall , is a new town that started construction more than a decade ago. It’s being developed by the Duchy of Cornwall, the private land portfolio run by the Prince of Wales It’s set to be home to 8,000 residents one day, along with a high street that could stop the decline of British town centres. Our teams worked through the night to locate the burst while carefully balancing the need to maintain water supplies for customers in the area. When I heard the word cancer it really hit me hard". Add to preferred sourc A grandad from Bury who went to the GP after noticing one symptom was later told by doctors he had a rugby-ball-sized tumour in his abdomen. Lee Bather, from Radcliffe , was diagnosed with kidney cancer in 2018 after the shock discovery of blood in his urine one night before bed The 68-year-old then saw his doctor, who referred him for tests which led to the discovery of a large tumour attached to part of his stomach, bowel and adrenal gland Lee said: "I went to see my GP and was referred immediately for an ultrasound. I could see for myself there was a huge mass on the screen "They said it was the size of a rugby ball and had been growing for around 12 years. When I heard the word cancer it really hit me hard. And the moment when you’re taken down the corridor for surgery not knowing if you’ll wake up and see your family again is really tough." The retired care worker underwent a nine-hour operation to remove the tumour, which was then taken away for research. He is now backing vital research into how type 2 diabetes could increase the risk of the disease

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Police issue update after officers swarm Manchester Arndale as boy, 13, stabbed A large number of emergency services vehicles were pictured outside the shopping centre on Tuesday evening Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blak Three boys who were arrested after a stabbing in Manchester city centre have been released on bail, police have confirmed Officers swarmed the Arndale shopping centre on Tuesday evening (October 27) following reports of a stabbing. Police taped off a lift in the shopping centre near the Roller's café while multiple police vehicles were seen on High Street and Withy Grove, including a forensics van A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said officers were called out to reports of a stabbing on Market Street , outside the Arndale on Withy Grove, at 7pm. A 13-year-old boy was taken to hospital from the scene with knife wounds Three boys - aged 14, 15 and 16 - were arrested on suspicion of affray. Another boy, aged 13, was arrested on suspicion of possession of a bladed article In an update issued today (October 29), a GMP spokesperson said three of the boys have since been released on bail. The other remains in hospital

Latest data shows that 28.2 per cent of eligible women in the region have not been screened in the past three years While uptake rose to 71.8 per cent between 2024 and 2025 - from 71.1 per cent the previous year - many women are still missing their screening The screening, also known as a mammogram, checks for signs of breast cancer - and can detect the disease before people may notice any signs or symptoms Women are invited to NHS breast screenings for the first time between the ages of 50 and 53, then every three years until they turn 71. Women aged 71 and over can self-refer for a screening if needed

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

candidates.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

candidates.evidence_text: An 'unparalleled' investigation shows a third of staff surveyed have experienced bad behaviour from senior officials A scathing report into Manchester City Council's working culture has found a prevailing “boys' club” mentality and widespread bad behaviour by senior staff. The internal document – that will be shared with council workers tomorrow and is based on a survey of nearly 1,200 staff – The report describes a culture at the council in which senior staff can act inappropriately with seeming impunity. Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

candidates.evidence_text: The new Transport Policing and Crime Command has been created to tackle crime and antisocial behaviour on the Bee Network The new squad will deliver a "significant increase" in visible policing and enforcement across the transport network, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said The dedicated unit, which will also cover the city's active travel routes and roads, has been formed with funding from the Mayor of Greater Manchester's budget It will be supported by control centre staff at GMP and Transport for Greater Manchester, which has access to CCTV cameras across bus stations, interchanges, tram stops and train stations Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson said the aim was to "make the roads and public transport among the safest in the UK" Bev Craig, Mayor of Greater Manchester said the move would "bring together up to 300 police and safety officers, with high-profile patrols across our roads and the Bee Network"

At 10.58am the service will begin A two-minute silence will be observed at 11am in tribute to those who have lost their lives in conflict. The start and conclusion of the silence will be marked by the firing of a maroon Following the service, veterans, military personnel and cadets will take part in a short return march across St Peter's Square to Mount Street

candidates.source_evidence: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges In December 2023 a trial was launched to embed two Citizens Advice case workers in two Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) run hospitals in Manchester - the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital and North Manchester General Hospital This was further expanded in June 2024 to include Wythenshawe Hospital, and the MRI in March 2025, and St Mary's in December 2025 with funding through MFT’s charity, as well as a damp and mould focused case worker funded through Manchester City Council The team of six Citizens Advice caseworkers are aimed at providing better wrap around care for patients and addressing the link we know exists between poor health, economic hardship and housing issues The trial has been a huge success with more than 1,500 people supported across the trial locations With more up to 3m patients contacts across MFT each year this presented a huge opportunity to reach people who may otherwise have not known about the services provided by Citizens Advice, or the support they were eligible to claim

A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts foll Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale is celebrating a blooming brilliant victory after striking gold at this year’s Britain in Bloom awards and being crowned the overall winner of the Town Centres and City Centres category Rochdale was placed ahead of Floral Godalming (Southeast), Shaftesbury in Bloom (South) and Sidcup Partners Limited (London) Rochdale in Bloom has a proud competition record, securing gold in 2018, being named Best Small City in 2022 and winning gold again for Rochdale town centre in 2024. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Streets in Bolton are set to be cleaner after the council invested in new equipment to tackle litter, leaves and fly-tipping New road sweepers have been purchased, bigger bins installed at key spots and handy equipment stores provided for volunteer litter pickers A fleet of road sweepers in various sizes are used by the council to remove leaves and litter, and there have been several recent additions One large sweeper has been added, making three in total, and these are vital for keeping roads and drains clear of leaves and twigs in autumn, which reduces the risk of flooding as well as keeping streets looking tidy Six smaller mechanical sweepers are used on pavements, with teams focusing on different areas of Bolton on a rotating schedule A new electrically powered pavement sweeper has also been brought in that can get into smaller spaces like cycle lanes, helping to keep them clean and safe to use

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . It can feel busy and overwhelming without much clarity on what’s actually working. This programme is about helping people step back, put the right foundations in plac The Monthly Marketing Programme is delivered through a structured monthly format, with immediate access to a starter guide on sign-up. candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: Joshua Reed-Cooper and Mike Thomas will bring regional French cooking and an extensive wine list to the former TNQ site this winter Go to Manchester's Finest X profile The duo behind Stockport’s Michelin-recognised Cantaloupe are opening a new French restaurant in the Northern Quarter Joshua Reed-Cooper and Mike Thomas will open Rasade at 108 High Street – the former site of long-standing bistro TNQ – this winter, with a menu inspired by regional French cooking and built around seasonal produce The new restaurant is the latest project from the pair, who have worked in some of the city’s most notable kitchens Cooper’s CV includes Where The Light Gets In , Adam Reid at The French and mana , while he also ran Tine, a pop-up kitchen at Blossom Street Social. candidates.lead: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867.
candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

The opening marks Open Restaurant Group’s 9th restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Di At the heart of the restaurant will be a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, placing guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors will feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, creating a setting designe Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallo t, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Demoted from weekend_activities to future_announcements: earliest date 2026-11-08 is 9 days out. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits. | Selection: Outside DeepSeek ranking board (soft max 90).

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester will mark Remembrance Sunday with its annual city centre service this November Honouring the service and sacrifice of members of the Armed Forces community, the commemorative event is open to all and will take place on Sun 8 Nov at the Manchester Cenotaph in St Peter’s Square between 10.30am and 12pm At 10.30am veterans, serving military personnel and cadets, led by the Greater Manchester Police Band, will march from John Dalton Street to the Cenotaph At 10.45am, the civic procession will set off from Mount Street, accompanied by the Scots Guards Association Pipe Band, making its way to the Cenotaph ahead of the service At 10.58am, the service will begin. A two-minute silence will be observed at 11am in tribute to those who have lost their lives in conflict. The start and conclusion of the silence will be marked by the firing of a maroon Following the service, veterans, military personnel and cadets will take part in a short return march across St Peter’s Square to Mount Street

Guests can expect Spanish-inspired small plates, generously loaded focaccias, charcuterie made for sharing and a drinks list packed with wine, beer Lunchtimes at El Gatito will centre around a selection of generously loaded focaccias, served Monday to Friday from 11am – 4pm, alongside a menu of Spanish-inspired small plates Available to eat in or take away, the focaccia lineup includes the signature ‘Iberico Club’, layering jamon serrano, salchichon, chorizo, manchego, roasted peppers, tomato, lettuce and salsa verde. A vegetarian option will also be available, featuring a twist on a traditional Spa By evening, El Gatito will switch focus to tapas, sharing plates and drinks, shaped by comforting flavours from Spain and across the Mediterranean. Highlights include melt-in-the-mouth slow-cooked Beef Short Rib and smoky Catalan Chorizo, sizzling Gambas Pil Pil, Manchego Churros Interiors will be kept purposely relaxed, with green booth seating, open-plan areas and bifold doors which open directly onto a dedicated terrace

candidates.evidence_text: A new exhibition at The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Open now, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

Written about the life and paintings of L. S. Lowry, it turned one of the region’s best-known artists into an unlikely pop culture ph Coming to Lowry this November, Matchstalks Remastered is a playful music-theatre performance inspired by the song, the artist and the city that connects them. Two performers, accompanied by live jazz musician Adam Fairhall and a record player, attempt to follow a constantly scrol As the record plays, movement, storytelling and slapstick collide. Kevin Egan and Michael Pinchbeck shift between performers, songwriters, Lowry himself and the familiar figures populating his paintings, using the structure of the original song to create a series of theatrical sc Along the way, the production follows Lowry’s footsteps around Manchester and plays with the way stories about artists are remembered and retold. How does a painting become a song? What happens when that song becomes theatre? And what gets lost, exaggerated or reinvented along th The performance also arrives in the year marking the 50th anniversary of Lowry’s death, offering an appropriately unconventional way to revisit an artist whose industrial landscapes remain closely tied to the identity of Greater Manchester

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Man United latest: 3 Michael Carrick replacements agreed upon as manager told how to save job Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has been handed a reprieve but faces a must-win Premier League clash against Chelsea on Saturday Add to preferr Manchester United have decided not to sack Michael Carrick for the time being. The 45-year-old was expected to be shown the door following a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth but will be in the dugout on Saturday against Chelsea Carrick's first full season in charge of United has started dismally. Eight Premier League games have been played so far and his side has won just once. They've also suffered four defeats and been held to three draws. Not to mention, they were sent packing from the Carabao Cup by After being beaten 3-0 by the Cherries, emergency discussions involving CEO Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox were held to decide whether Carrick would be sacked The decision was taken to afford the manager additional time , with suitable replacements in short supply. But two United legends have agreed upon three names they think would be good Carrick replacements. The Manchester Evening News brings you the latest from Old Trafford Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt have selected three managers they believe would be suitable to step in should Carrick be dismissed. And one of those names was former team-mate Roy Keane

The 45-year-old was expected to be shown the door following a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth but will be in the dugout on Saturday against Chelsea Carrick's first full season in charge of United has started dismally. Eight Premier League games have been played so far and his side has won just once. They've also suffered four defeats and been held to three draws. Not to mention, they were sent packing from the Carabao Cup by After being beaten 3-0 by the Cherries, emergency discussions involving CEO Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox were held to decide whether Carrick would be sacked The decision was taken to afford the manager additional time , with suitable replacements in short supply. But two United legends have agreed upon three names they think would be good Carrick replacements. The Manchester Evening News brings you the latest from Old Trafford Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt have selected three managers they believe would be suitable to step in should Carrick be dismissed. And one of those names was former team-mate Roy Keane

candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC I played alongside Wayne Rooney and Sergio Aguero - it's clear who was the best One star with experience on both sides of the Manchester divide has picked his ideal striking partner Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Tom Sunderland Sports Carlos Tevez has planted his flag in the sand by choosing Wayne Rooney over Sergio Aguero as his best strike partner. The Argentinian had vast experience playing alongside both Manchester icons but picked the United legend as his favourite Tevez holds a mixed reputation around Manchester after achieving huge success at Manchester United before jumping ship to rivals Manchester City . A hugely productive two-year loan at Old Trafford saw Tevez clinch consecutive Premier League titles, the Champions League , the Cara That was before he made the controversial decision to move to the Etihad in 2009 , where he eventually linked up with his Argentina team-mate. But despite the bond he shared with his countryman at City, he couldn't look beyond 'Wazza' while speaking to another former colleague, R "They are very different," said Tevez during an appearance on the Rio Ferdinand Presents channel when asked who was the better partner. "They are different but for me the best player...I don’t know how to say. Best partner. Yeah. The best partner." Tevez, who retired in 2022, spent an identical two-season spell playing alongside each player. Aguero didn't arrive at City until 2011 when Tevez was already an established figure, with his arrival possibly playing a role in the latter eventually leaving for Juventus

Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Our Partner experts will be on Monex is a global financial services group with more than 40 years of experience helping businesses navigate global markets through foreign exchange expertise, market insights, and risk management solutions.
